outcome: Controlled redirect fetching implemented and JVM regressions pass; Android hardware behavior remains unverified.

EmbeddedVideoActivity.kt: Both WebView HTTP request interceptor overloads return controlled responses rather than null/unchecked WebView networking.
Modern interceptor forwards the requested GET/HEAD method and public request headers to RestrictedResourceFetcher.
HTTPS page subresources are subject to an explicit secure-context guard; existing MIXED_CONTENT_NEVER_ALLOW and SSL handler cancellation remain.
Invalid Android WebResourceResponse metadata closes the controlled stream and returns an empty 502, never an unchecked network fallback.
RestrictedResourceFetcher.kt: Initial URL and every redirect destination are checked before opening a connection; automatic redirects are disabled. Five redirects/six requests maximum.
Connect timeout is 10000 ms and read timeout is 15000 ms per connection; no TLS verifier/trust-manager overrides or authorization retry path were added.
HTTPS downgrade redirects and HTTP subresources in an HTTPS context fail closed before requesting the destination.

NativeUrlPolicy remains the base policy. Additional resource-only filtering rejects obvious live/channel/public-list route families and removed public-list action aliases, while retaining private collections and episode playlists.

Only GET/HEAD and a small public request-header allowlist are supported. Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization and arbitrary private headers are not copied. Origin/Referer are stripped after crossing scheme/host/port and are never restored later in the chain.

Body remains streaming and owns/disconnects its connection when closed. MIME/charset, final HTTP status, content length/range, CORS and non-hop response metadata are retained. Set-Cookie and hop-by-hop response headers are removed.

Malformed/missing redirects and transport failures produce empty 502; exhausted redirects produce 508; blocked policy/mixed-content destinations produce 403. Unexpected 3xx/invalid statuses cannot escape to Android. Reason phrases are nonblank printable ASCII.

verification.serialization: Runner acquires /root/reelbox/.tooling.lock internally; no outer flock was used.
verification.compiler: Offline cached Kotlin 2.2.21 compiler, JVM target 17, 256 MB heap/192 MB metaspace; no Gradle or APK build.
actual_local_http_evidence: Server hit counters show blocked redirect targets were not contacted for GET or HEAD, including news/support/updater/APK/vendor/Telegram/live/channel/public-list destinations.
Allowed relative redirect returns exact public script body/MIME/charset/CORS metadata; private collection and episode-playlist paths remain permitted.
GET and HEAD survive a safe 307 redirect with Range/If-Range and exact 206 Content-Range/Content-Length metadata; GET body is exact and HEAD body empty.
Cross-host loopback redirects (127.0.0.1 -> localhost -> 127.0.0.1) strip sensitive context and never restore it; credential/private headers are absent at every fixture server.
401/403/451/404/416 statuses and bodies pass through without retries; unsupported methods do not contact the server.
deterministic_connection_seam_evidence: Connections have finite connect/read timeout settings and redirects disabled before reading status.
HTTPS downgrade/mixed-content targets are not opened; injected SSLHandshakeException/IOException/SocketTimeoutException fail closed with connection cleanup.
Streaming does not eagerly read the body; closing the response closes the payload and disconnects the connection.
Invalid status codes, unhandled 3xx and invalid reason phrases cannot produce forbidden Android response metadata.
verification.source_wiring_check: Passed: both interceptor overloads use the helper, no return-null fallback, method/header and secure-context wiring present, SSL cancellation and fail-closed adapter present. This is text/source verification, not an Android execution test.
tdd_observations: Initial runner failed compilation because the previous partial implementation did not provide the existing tests' openConnection/secureContext seam.
After completing the transport seam/timeouts, the original six fixture groups passed.
New invalid-status regression failed with -1 escaping unchanged, then passed after status validation.
New exclusion regression failed by following /live/channel.m3u8, then passed after resource-only removed-family filtering.
Full helper suite passed while integration check correctly failed on the old return-null interceptor; wiring was then replaced.
Invalid reason-phrase regression failed before sanitization; the final complete runner passed.

remaining_checks: Controlled Android WebView redirect-marker regression, actual media range seeking, TLS/access-denial rendering, fullscreen/back/file chooser and activity recreation.

Redirected HTML/CSS document effective-URL/base-relative-resource and cross-origin/CORS behavior on the actual WebView: the helper reports effectiveUrl but WebResourceResponse has no final-URL field, and these browser semantics were not established by the JVM HTTP tests.
Device TLS trust/hostname behavior: normal platform transport is retained, but the TLS failure regression uses an injected exception, not a real device TLS handshake.

scope_and_issues: No MainActivity, Cast, service, Gradle, Dart, completed-media, manifest or NativeUrlPolicy edits were made by this task. No accounts, external credentials or real cookies were used.
No unsafe TLS workaround or access-denial bypass was introduced. POST/OPTIONS/authenticated embeds intentionally fail closed rather than offering account/CORS bypass support.
The runner now bounds compiler/test subprocess runtime and keeps its existing internal tooling lock.
Host free disk was 145 MB at final inspection; no full native build was attempted and no unrelated artifacts were deleted.

Optional web_extract backend could not retrieve Android documentation; the official Android WebResourceResponse API was retrieved directly over HTTPS to confirm valid status ranges and unsupported 3xx responses.
